Complain
kŏm-plān´
v. (to express grief or grievance; to murmur; rendering Hebrew siach, anan, and bakah, Greek mempsimoiros)
Latin complangere, to beat the breast. Job's Hebrew is to pour out a meditation; Numbers' is to murmur; Lamentations asks what a living man has to complain of.

Biblical Definition

Job: “Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul” (Job 7:11). Jeremiah: “Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” (Lam 3:39). In the wilderness, “when the people complained, it displeased the LORD: and the LORD heard it; and his anger was kindled” (Num 11:1). Jude's apostates are “murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts” (Jud 1:16). And the blessing: “that there be no complaining in our streets” (Psa 144:14).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines complain as to utter expressions of grief; to lament; to utter expressions of censure or resentment; to murmur; to find fault; to make a formal charge.

expand to see more

COMPLAIN, v.i. To utter expressions of grief; to lament.

2. To utter expressions of censure or resentment; to murmur; to find fault.

3. To utter expressions of uneasiness or pain.

4. To charge; to accuse of an offense; to present with an accusation.

Key Scripture

Lam 3:39 — "Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?"

Job 7:11 — "Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul."

Num 11:1 — "And when the people complained, it displeased the LORD: and the LORD heard it; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the LORD burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp."

Jud 1:16 — "These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men's persons in admiration because of advantage."

Psa 144:14 — "That our oxen may be strong to labour; that there be no breaking in, nor going out; that there be no complaining in our streets."

Modern Corruption

Complaint to God and complaint about God are confused, and Job did the first and Israel the second.

expand to see more

Scripture has two complainings and judges them oppositely. Job complained in the bitterness of his soul, and he complained to God — the whole book is his case laid before the One he could not find — and at the end God said Job had spoken of Him the thing that is right. Israel complained in the wilderness, and the complaint was about God, to each other, in the tents, and the fire of the LORD burnt among them. The difference is the address. Lamentations 3:39 is the sentence that ends the second kind: wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins? — a man alive is a man under mercy, and a man punished for sin is a man who has received less than he earned. Jude's complainers are the second kind grown into a party, and Psalm 144 promises the streets a day without them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew siach (H7878), to muse, complain, pour out; anan (H596), to murmur, complain; bakah (H1058), to weep; Greek mempsimoiros (G3202), a complainer of his lot.

expand to see more

Hebrew siach (H7878) — to complain, meditate; Job 7:11, Psalm 77:3, 142:2.

Hebrew anan (H596) — to murmur, complain; Lamentations 3:39, Numbers 11:1.

Greek mempsimoiros (G3202) — complainer; Jude 1:16 only; Hebrew tsevachah (H6682), outcry, complaining; Psalm 144:14.

Usage

"“I will complain in the bitterness of my soul” — Job, to God."

"“When the people complained, it displeased the LORD” — Israel, about God."

"“Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” — the end of the second kind."
